labels.label: bzdef:c3s1d3_variete_appui
labels.notes: IsVarieteAppui W S := (S ∩ W).Nonempty ∧ (A ∈ S∩W → FW W A B → B ∈ S∩W). That is Déf. 3 word for word (variété linéaire = AffineSubspace ℝ E, F_W = FW from strict Facettes). The α-form of l.192–193 is isVarieteAppui_iff_alphaW under W convex, the context of the whole section. On the commentary: isVarieteAppui_top_iff (whole space, iff W ≠ ∅, degenerate case honestly isolated), isVarieteAppui_affineSpan_facette (a facette's support), and antidiag_appui_not_support. The last is real and non-vacuous: x+y=0 meets [0,1]² in {0}, a vertex, so it is a variété d'appui, and its support is not antidiag. This is exactly the commentary's finite-dimensional « S ∩ W ait un support distinct de S ». Bourbaki's equivalence (isVarieteAppui_iff_openSegment: an open segment of W meeting S has both ends in S) is the standard Bourbaki EVT II wording, equivalent to « contenu dans S » for an affine S. The REPORT disclosed it as a question. Instances checked: lineY0_isVarieteAppui (y=0 is an edge of the square, true) and not_diag_isVarieteAppui (the witness (1/2,1/2) α (1/2,0) leaves the diagonal, true).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p5_appui_facette_dim_finie
labels.notes: exists_facette_support_inter_eq carries exactly the paper's hypotheses: Convex W, FiniteDimensional (affineSpan W).direction, IsVarieteAppui W L. Its conclusion is the paper's: ∃ F, IsFacette W F ∧ affineSpan F ∩ W = L ∩ W. The stronger form exists_facette_support_inter_eq_of_finiteDimensional needs only affineSpan (L ∩ W) finite-dimensional and additionally gives affineSpan F = affineSpan (L ∩ W), the paper proof's S. The proof route (a facette of maximal finrank instead of a « point interne ») is the closer's own; the kernel checks it and the statement does not depend on it.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s1r2_support_interieur_fermeture
labels.notes: 1° remarque_facette_interieur: ∃ F facette, affineSpan F = affineSpan W ∧ F = intrinsicInterior ℝ W. It adds W.Nonempty, which is legitimate: for W = ∅ there is no facette, so the sentence is false, and the Remark sits in Prop. 5's context, where a variété d'appui forces W ≠ ∅. The SCOPE discloses this. The topology reading is sound. The statement is universally quantified over every Hausdorff TVS structure on E. intrinsicInterior depends only on the subspace topology of the finite-dimensional affineSpan W, which is the canonical one for any such structure. So the Lean statement implies the paper's reading, and the topology-free core exists_facette_support_eq is also given. 2° remarque_fermeture_compacte gives, for IsCompact W, finite dimension and L a variété d'appui: ∃ F facette with affineSpan F ∩ W = L ∩ W ∧ L ∩ W = closure F ∧ IsCompact (closure F). This is the [sic] « fermeture compacte E de F » read as F̄, and the scan (PDF p. 34) prints « E » as the transcription says. inter_eq_closure_facette strengthens this to every such F and to W only closed. The closure is taken in E, but F lies in the closed finite-dimensional affineSpan F, so it agrees with the closure in the support.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p6_alpha_induit
labels.notes: alphaW_inter_iff: AlphaW (W ∩ L) A B ↔ A ∈ L ∧ B ∈ L ∧ AlphaW W A B, for W convex and any L. This is « α(W′) est induite par α(W) » with no non-emptiness hypothesis, so it is ≥ the paper under either reading of the printed « = ∅ ». The scan OCR (PDF p. 34) shows « W'= Wr\L=0 », consistent with the transcription's [sic], and the reading ≠ ∅ is the only non-trivial one. alphaW_induit carries the read hypothesis (unused, harmless). facetteOf_inter_eq formalizes the proof's consequence (facette relative to W = facette relative to L ∩ W, for L a variété d'appui), correctly.
